title: Why fzlt
subtitle: Four letters, picked so nothing else answers to them.
lead: Fizlet™ is the name you remember. fzlt™ is its short mark: the npm scope, and the mark for tight spaces. We picked it on purpose, so nobody mixes it up with anything else. Today you install Fizlet with `npm i @fzlt/core`.

items: **No vowels.** fzlt is not a real word, and not a misspelling of one.
**A z.** It is one of the least-used letters in English.
**Nothing autocorrects into it.** And nobody types it by accident.
**It is short.** Four lowercase letters, quick to type in a command.

body.text: Fizlet stays the name in prose and headlines. fzlt is always lowercase, and lives where space is tight: npm, badges, the command line.
The package is `@fzlt/core`. Bricks are subpaths: `import { arcade } from "@fzlt/core/arcade"`.
Plain `fzlt` is requested from npm, and not ours yet. Until it is, the alias works: `npm i fzlt@npm:@fzlt/core`.
The GitHub org is [github.com/fizlet ↗](https://github.com/fizlet); the code stays at coded-dot-design/fizlet for now. fzlt.dev and fzlt.app are planned, as redirects to fizlet.com.
Fizlet and fzlt are trademarks of Chris Cooley.
